newsitem.title: ITALY: Olivetti CEO in probe of group statements.
newsitem.headline: Olivetti CEO in probe of group statements.

text.p: Francesco Caio, the chief executive of crisis-hit Italian information technology group Olivetti, has been put under preliminary investigation by magistrates, judicial sources said on Monday.

The investigation, conducted by magistrates in the town of Ivrea where Olivetti is based, is a first step which could lead to a full-scale criminal investigation into public statements made by Olivetti on its finances.

Ivrea magistrates questioned former Olivetti director general Renzo Francesconi into the early hours of Saturday morning as a "person informed of the facts" following his comments earlier this month which cast doubt on the accuracy of the group's first half results for this year.

Francesconi resigned from the loss-making group nearly two weeks ago shortly after the company announced that its chairman for the past 18 years Carlo De Benedetti was standing down and that it had made a 440.2 billion lire loss ($288.5 million) for the first six months.
Francesconi has also been questioned by stock market watchdog Consob which is conducting its own inquiry into Olivetti's finances.
Caio may face questioning in the coming days by two Ivrea based investigators Alberto Braghin and Lorenzo Fornace, the sources said.
